Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick post-demo recap and a couple of asks so we can size correctly before the pilot:

Recap / constraints you mentioned:
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + contextual retrieval for agents (short prompts avg ~120–160 tokens).
- Streaming: yes for the agent-facing summarization flows (partial updates important).
- Latency targets: p95 <= 300–400ms for interactive agent flows; background batch tasks can tolerate higher latency.
- Steady QPS: ~40–50 QPS; peak QPS: up to ~180–220 QPS during business hours spike.
- Concurrent in-flight requests observed today: ~50–70.

Can you confirm the following numbers and share a sample traffic CSV if possible?
- Average tokens per response (gen only): 
- Peak QPS and typical steady QPS by hour (one-week sample if available)
- Percent of requests that need streaming vs non-streaming
- Any long-tail requests > 500 tokens

If you can attach a short sample (CSV is fine) with timestamp, tokens_out, request_type, we’ll map to tokens/sec and propose an initial Dedicated configuration and pilot plan. I’ve copied Rafael and Marissa to help with sizing & pricing.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share sample traffic CSV (or permission to load a short sample to our sizing spreadsheet).
2) Redwood runs an initial throughput calc + recommended pool (we’ll show tokens/sec, expected in-flight concurrency at p95 SLO, and fallback model variants).
3) Sync call if anything looks off.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming numbers from our side and attaching a quick sample.

Quick answers:
- Average tokens per generated response: 140 tokens (median ~120, 90th pct ~260).
- Peak QPS: 200–220 (we see these spikes across the noon hour and end-of-day wrap-ups).
- Steady QPS: 40–50 (overnight and outside business hours).
- Typical concurrent in-flight requests during peak: ~60.
- Streaming: ~30% of requests require streaming (agent sessions); the rest are non-streaming synchronous summarizations.
- Long-tail: about 2% of requests exceed 500 tokens (summaries + conversation stitching).

Attached: finex_sample_traffic.csv — contains 48 hours of anonymized timestamps, request_type (stream/nonstream), tokens_out.

Latency SLOs: for interactive agent flows we prefer p95 <= 300ms if possible; if not achievable we can stretch to 400ms but want to understand cost tradeoffs. Background batch jobs are fine at p95 <= 2s.

Let us know if you need additional columns in the CSV.

Neha / Marissa — quick sizing notes based on the CSV Alex sent and the confirmed numbers. Attaching a short PDF with the math. Highlights below: (internal)

Sizing math (peak figures):
- Peak QPS: 220
- Avg tokens / response: 140
- Peak tokens/sec = 220 QPS * 140 tokens = 30,800 tokens/sec
- Steady tokens/sec = 45 QPS * 140 tokens = 6,300 tokens/sec
- Target p95 latency: 300ms -> expected in-flight concurrency = peak QPS * latency_seconds = 220 * 0.3 = 66 in-flight requests (matches reported ~60).

Recommendations / notes:
1) Dedicated pool: start with 3 x high-throughput inference instances (e.g., q4_merged / 8x A10 equivalent throughput) configured with low-latency kernel paths and streaming-optimized worker threads. This gives us headroom to meet p95 ~300ms for most requests while handling bursts.
2) Streaming: route streaming requests to the same pool but enable dedicated smaller batch windows for streaming (reduce batching delay) and a higher concurrency cap. Because ~30% of traffic is streaming, we recommend tuning the autoscaler to keep a small warm buffer for streaming spikes.
3) Fallbacks: configure a slightly smaller but cheaper quantized model variant for non-critical (background) flows to reduce cost during non-peak hours.
4) Pilot plan: one-week pilot sized at ~20% of peak (approx 6k tokens/sec sustained) to validate end-to-end latencies and autoscaling.

Next actions:
- I attached redwood_sizing_notes.pdf with the detailed calc and a sample autoscaler config.
- Rafael -> will sync with infra on estimated instance SKU and price points (cc Marissa for pricing).
- Neha -> share the one-week pilot request with Finex and confirm sampling window.
